concerns.text: The plan uses a two‑proportion Z‑test (continuity corrected) to compare the empirical Type I error rates of CC versus MI/IPW at the identified tipping point, treating the error‑rate estimates as independent samples. In reality, each method is applied to the *same* simulated dataset per iteration, so the resulting error indicators are positively correlated. A standard two‑proportion Z‑test assumes independent binomial samples, making the p‑values anti‑conservative and the comparison statistically invalid.

The same two‑proportion Z‑test is used to assess whether `error_CC > 2 × error_MI` (or IPW). This test evaluates a difference in proportions, not a ratio, so it does not directly test the stated hypothesis about a >2× inflation. A more appropriate approach would be a paired test (e.g., McNemar’s test on per‑iteration rejection concordance) or a bootstrap confidence interval for the ratio of error rates.
